The fault is centered in [scripts/affiliate_server.py](/app/scripts/affiliate_server.py:115). `PrioritizedISBN` stores identifiers in `isbn`; its generated equality compares priority and timestamp instead of the identifier, and it is unhashable. `Submit.GET` also checks an ASIN string against queue objects, so that check cannot prevent duplicate submissions.

The fix should introduce `PrioritizedIdentifier` with an `identifier` field, identifier-only equality and hash, a `stage_import` flag, and JSON-safe serialization of every field. It must carry `stage_import` through `amazon_lookup` into `process_amazon_batch`, which currently stages every fetched product. Backward compatibility needs particular care: [existing tests](/app/scripts/tests/test_affiliate_server.py:133) import `PrioritizedISBN` and construct it with `isbn=`; an alias alone would not preserve that keyword.

No source or tests were changed. The developer instruction for this run explicitly limits my role to fault localization, despite the request to edit files. I recorded the findings in `.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md`.

Implemented `PrioritizedIdentifier` with a generic identifier, `stage_import`, identifier-based equality and hashing, and JSON serialization of all fields. The affiliate workflow now deduplicates queued identifiers and stages only products requested for import. Existing `PrioritizedISBN` imports and `isbn` construction remain supported.

Verification: 18 affiliate server tests pass; Ruff and `git diff --check` pass.

VERDICT: FIX

The applied patch has two workflow defects in [affiliate_server.py](/app/scripts/affiliate_server.py):

- Lines 515–521 return a cached product before handling `stage_import=True`. If an earlier request cached the product without staging it, a later import request never queues an import. Stage the cached product or schedule import before returning.
- Lines 528–535 deduplicate a queued identifier without upgrading its priority. A later `high_priority=true` request can remain behind low priority work. Update the queue entry and restore heap ordering.

`pytest -q scripts/tests/test_affiliate_server.py` **passed: 18 tests**. `git diff --check` passed. These passing tests do not cover the two cases above. No project code or tests were changed during this review.

Fixed both reviewed workflow defects in [affiliate_server.py](/app/scripts/affiliate_server.py): import requests now stage cached products before returning, and repeat requests upgrade a queued identifier’s priority while preserving heap order. Added regression tests for both cases.

Verification: `pytest -q scripts/tests/test_affiliate_server.py` passed (20 tests); `git diff --check` passed.
